stem.text: Consider the curve (x^2 + 6x + 5)(2y - y^2) = 12, for which dy/dx = -(x + 3)(2y - y^2)/((x^2 + 6x + 5)(1 - y)). At the point P in the second quadrant the tangent line to the curve is vertical. What is the x-coordinate of P?

worked_solution.text: A vertical tangent needs the denominator of dy/dx to be zero with the numerator nonzero. The denominator is zero when y = 1, x = -1, or x = -5.
At x = -1 or x = -5 the factor x^2 + 6x + 5 is 0, so the left side of the curve equation is 0, not 12. Neither x-value belongs to a point of the curve.
Substitute y = 1: 2y - y^2 = 1, so x^2 + 6x + 5 = 12 and x^2 + 6x - 7 = 0, which gives x = 1 or x = -7.
At (-7, 1) the numerator is -(-4)(1) = 4, which is nonzero, so the tangent is vertical there. The point (-7, 1) is in the second quadrant and (1, 1) is in the first, so the x-coordinate of P is -7.
